enhanced_title: Letters, Loo, and a Reel Refused
description: Darcy's growing fascination with Elizabeth becomes evident as they engage in intellectual sparring over the nature of humility and friendship. Miss Bingley's jealousy reaches a fever pitch, leading her to mock Elizabeth's connections in a desperate bid to distract Darcy.

analysis_entries.anchor: repeatedly calling off his attention by messages to his sister.
analysis_entries.note: Miss Bingley's constant interruptions of Darcy's letter-writing highlight her performative intimacy with his family and her desperate need for his attention, which he receives with 'perfect unconcern.'

analysis_entries.anchor: Nothing is more deceitful,” said Darcy, “than the appearance of humility.
analysis_entries.note: Darcy's cynical view of humility as a form of 'indirect boast' reveals his disdain for social pretension and his preference for blunt, intellectual honesty, even at the expense of his friend Bingley.

analysis_entries.anchor: To yield without conviction is no compliment to the understanding of either.
analysis_entries.note: This statement encapsulates Darcy's rigid moral and intellectual framework: he values conviction above social harmony, a trait that makes him both formidable and, to Elizabeth, initially insufferable.

analysis_entries.anchor: perceive that he was rather offended, and therefore checked her laugh.
analysis_entries.note: Elizabeth's decision to check her laugh at Darcy's expense shows a growing, perhaps unconscious, respect for his feelings, marking a subtle shift in their dynamic from purely adversarial to one of cautious observation.

analysis_entries.anchor: bewitched by any woman as he was by her.
analysis_entries.note: The word 'bewitched' is significant in Austen's vocabulary; it suggests an attraction that Darcy cannot logically explain or control, particularly given his strong feelings about the 'inferiority' of her connections.

analysis_entries.anchor: planning his happiness in such an alliance.
analysis_entries.note: Miss Bingley's mocking of a potential marriage between Darcy and Elizabeth is a classic case of dramatic irony: her attempts to make the idea ridiculous only serve to fix it more firmly in Darcy's (and the reader's) mind.
Elizabeth's witty exit from the walk in the shrubbery leaves the others 'grouped' in their own social artifice, while she escapes into the freedom and 'rejoicing' of her own company.

quote_entries.anchor: Nothing is more deceitful,” said Darcy, “than the appearance of humility.
quote_entries.callout: <Callout variant="quote" title="Darcy on Humility">“Nothing is more deceitful,” said Darcy, “than the appearance of humility. It is often only carelessness of opinion, and sometimes an indirect boast.”</Callout>

quote_entries.anchor: To yield without conviction is no compliment to the understanding of either.
quote_entries.callout: <Callout variant="quote" title="Yielding and Conviction">“To yield without conviction is no compliment to the understanding of either.”</Callout>
<Callout variant="quote" title="Darcy’s Voice">“Upon my word, I cannot exactly explain the matter—Darcy must speak for himself.”</Callout>

quote_entries.anchor: I am not particularly speaking of such a case as you have supposed
quote_entries.callout: <Callout variant="quote" title="Elizabeth’s Distinction">“I am not particularly speaking of such a case as you have supposed about Mr. Bingley. We may as well wait, perhaps, till the circumstance occurs.”</Callout>
<Callout variant="quote" title="A Bold Refusal">“I have, therefore, made up my mind to tell you that I do not want to dance a reel at all; and now despise me if you dare.”</Callout>
<Callout variant="quote" title="Darcy’s Admission">“Indeed I do not dare.”</Callout>

quote_entries.anchor: The picturesque would be spoilt by admitting a fourth.
quote_entries.callout: <Callout variant="quote" title="The Picturesque Trio">“No, no; stay where you are. You are charmingly grouped, and appear to uncommon advantage. The picturesque would be spoilt by admitting a fourth. Good-bye.”</Callout>
